text:
alex: Heads-up — after landing the FP8 kernel selection patch this morning, we saw a 12-18% throughput regression on Mistral-7B@seq1024 compared to INT8 fallback. Perf tests attached in the CI artifacts. Notable: FP8 forward is slightly faster but the quantized matmul path is causing more memory stalls at batch sizes >8.

mira: Ack. Do you have the flamegraphs and the kernel selection trace? Can you paste the profiling snippet?

alex: Pasting the stripped timeline from perf-bot: 
```
kernel_selector: chosen=fp8_matmul_v2 (latency_ms=0.82, mem_stalls=0.18)
kv_cache: hit_rate=0.92
batching: avg_batch=6.4, tail_p99=280ms
fallbacks: 14% requests -> int8_matmul_v1 when OOMs detected
```

perf-bot: Automated profile URL: https://ci.redwood.ai/flat/profile/1750001234

sam: My hypothesis: the FP8 kernels require stricter input alignment and end up misaligned in our multi-stream tiled allocator for larger batches. Two actionable items: 1) tweak batching heuristic to prefer smaller sub-batches for fp8_matmul_v2 when seq>512; 2) try fp8 kernel with packed-weights layout.

june: Also seeing some KV-cache churn on generation tests when we fall back across model variants (qwen->mistral hybrid route). If KV cache pointers change layout between kernels (fp8 vs int8) we could be invalidating more cache entries than we think. That inflates latency.

mira: Can we reproduce deterministically? If it's alignment, a microbenchmark that varies batch and seq with pinned allocator should show throughput cliffs. I can run microbench this afternoon.

alex: I ran a small reproduce harness: 
```bash
# run batch sweep
for B in 1 2 4 8 16; do 
  ./microbench --model mistral-7b --seq 1024 --batch $B --kernels fp8_matmul_v2,int8_matmul_v1 --repeat 30 
done
```
Results: B=1..4 fp8 wins by 5-12% B=8 fp8 ~= int8 B=16 int8 +18%
```

sam: Ok that matches alignment hypothesis. Two experiments: 1) enable packed-weights FP8 layout (cheap kernel flag), 2) change batching heuristic to cap fp8_matmul_v2 to batch<=8 when seq>=768. Which do you want me to try?

alex: Try packed-weights first; if that drops stalls it's purely kernel-layout. If not, we should implement the batching cap. Also record KV cache pointer behavior.

perf-bot: Profiling summary for latest run (1750001234): [fp8_matmul_v2] cpu_wait 14%, mem_stalls 21%, gpu_util 78% | [int8_matmul_v1] cpu_wait 9%, mem_stalls 12%, gpu_util 68%

june: Regarding KV cache: I instrumented cache descriptors and saw pointer churn when model_variant changed from "mistral-q4f16" -> "mistral-fp8" during fallback. We should add a cache compatibility layer that keeps stable base pointers and just swaps quantization metadata.

mira: Good catch. That'll help latency and correctness for pinned sessions. Also, calibration: when we switched int8 calibration to per-channel symmetric vs per-tensor asymmetric for Qwen models, we saw a small 1-2% quality delta but a 10% speed boost due to simpler dequant path. Need to capture that tradeoff in model profiles.

alex: Agreed — proposal: share model-specific quant profiles in /configs/quant-profiles.json (read-only at runtime) with keys: model_name, preferred_kernel, cal_method, max_batch_for_kernel, notes. Example: 
```json
{"model": "mistral-7b", "preferred_kernel": "fp8_matmul_v2", "cal_method": "per-channel-symmetric", "max_batch_for_kernel": 8, "notes": "use packed-weights flag if available"}
```

sam: Sounds right. Also add a field for fallback_order: ["fp8_matmul_v2","int8_matmul_v1","fp4_experimental"]. This will let smart routing pick perf/cost fallbacks.

ops-bot: Rolling experiment deploy: canary=5% eng-runtime on prod-south with fp8 packed-weights flag enabled for mistral-7b. Monitor p99 latency and error-rate. Link: https://deploy.redwood.ai/canary/1750001234

mira: I'll run the microbench with the packed-weights flag and post numbers. If we still see regressions, next step is batching heuristic change and adding the KV compatibility shim.

alex: Thanks — tagging @sam and @june for follow-ups. Will update CI perf thresholds after the canary. :thumbsup:
